follow-up time: Prospective follow-up survey conducted in April and May 2020
study type: Monocentric retrospective cohort study with prospective follow-up
exposure: Type of suture used in laparoscopic myomectomy (conventional vs. barbed)
cohort: 343 women who underwent laparoscopic myomectomy for uterine leiomyomas
finding: The study found no significant difference in reproductive outcomes, including pregnancy rates and complications, between women who underwent laparoscopic myomectomy with barbed sutures compared to conventional sutures.
mod_finding: There were no significant differences in the mode of delivery or pregnancy outcomes between women who underwent laparoscopic myomectomy with barbed sutures compared to conventional sutures.
